title: Distinguish git-level errors from diff3 conflicts; fail safe without guessing content
context: The grounding merge driver silently corrupted files in two ways: (1) regex matching was too brittle, leaving conflict markers in place but reporting success; (2) git errors like binary-file detection (exit 255, empty stdout) were misinterpreted as 'clean merge', truncating files to zero bytes.
decision: When git merge-file exits outside 1-127 (the valid conflict-count range), treat it as a git-level error and return write: null instead of attempting to parse stdout. This signals that the file should not be modified, leaving it for human resolution. Additionally, added post-replacement marker scanning: if any diff3 marker survives after resolution logic runs, unconditionally treat it as unresolved.
consequences: Binary files and git-level errors now fail safely; the file remains untouched instead of being truncated
No more silent data loss when git detects unmergeable content
Genuine conflicts are reliably detected even in edge cases (empty hunks, CRLF line endings, unforeseen hunk shapes)
Two independent defenses: regex anchoring (prevent missed hunks) and marker scan (catch unrecognized hunk shapes)
alternatives_rejected: Attempt to parse and recover from all git errors—too fragile; git's error modes are not guaranteed to have parseable stdout
Rely on regex pattern matching alone—fails silently on future hunk shapes
Coerce all git output to empty string and assume clean merge—loses information about why git failed
